• An exact output format
• A fallback tag, e.g. 'Other'

reddit_title: How to get consistent summaries and tags from Notion AI autofill properties (setup + example tag prompt)
reddit_post:
Notion AI autofill properties can summarize database entries, pull out specific facts and tag them. Out of the box, though, the results are often vague or inconsistent. This setup fixes most of that.

**1. Check access first**
Whether you have Notion AI, and how much you can use it, depends on your plan. Notion has also changed how it packages AI over time. Check the pricing page and your workspace settings before you build something your team depends on.

**2. Put the raw text in the page body**
Autofill reads the page content, so an empty page body gets you generic output. Click the arrow next to the database's New button, create a template with an "Original message" heading and set it as the default. Then paste the full email, form answers or review under that heading for every entry.

For long threads, trim signatures and quoted replies and put the key message first. Long pages can get summarized poorly.

**3. Pick the right property type** (click + at the right end of the property header row)
- **AI summary**: a general overview.
- **AI key info**: one named type of fact. Be specific. "Deadline, budget and requested deliverable" works, but "important details" gives you vague output.
- **AI custom autofill**: your own prompt. This is the one to use for tags.

**4. Write the tag prompt like a spec**
Include a closed list of allowed tags, an exact output format, a fallback tag and one example. Something like:

> Classify this request using ONLY one of these tags: Bug, Feature Request, Billing, Question, Other.
> Output only the tag name, nothing else.
> If none of the tags fit, output Other.
> Example: "I was charged twice this month" → Billing

Don't use tag names that appear inside other tag names (e.g. "Urgent" and "Not Urgent"). A Contains filter would match both.

**5. Test on 10–20 existing pages**
Autofill works on entries you already have. You can generate one cell at a time or all pages at once from the property's menu. Start small: compare each result with the tag you would have picked, tighten the definition wherever it's wrong, then test again. Testing small matters even more if your plan limits AI usage.

**6. Auto-update or manual refresh**
"Auto-update on page edits" regenerates the value after a page is edited, though not always instantly. Use it for entries that keep changing, like leads that get new call notes. Leave it off while you're testing and for entries that rarely change.

**7. Filtered views + a human-owned final tag**
Build views like "Urgent requests" or "Negative feedback" with a Contains or Starts with filter on the AI property. Then add a "Final Type" Select property that only a person sets. Use that one for reporting and anything that matters.

**What about Select/Multi-select properties?**
Autofill started out producing text, and newer versions of Notion have expanded where you can use it. Open the settings of a Select property in your workspace and see whether an AI autofill option appears. If it doesn't, write the tags to a text property and filter with Contains or Starts with.

Disclosure: this is condensed from a guide I published on The Wealth Ascent. Everything you need is above, but the full version with an FAQ is here if it helps: {URL}
